Elma, who joined as a publicity asset, ends the mission as an astronaut whose contribution to its survival was practical, and she and Parker close the voyage as colleagues who finally understand each other. Nathaniel is still on Earth, where the climate emergency that justified the entire program grinds on. Mars is now the beginning of the colony the coalition promised rather than a destination reached, and the work of building it is entirely ahead of them.

characters.description: The narrator, a sixteen-year-old girl living with thyroid cancer that has spread to her lungs, which forces her to carry a portable oxygen tank and breathe through a nasal cannula. Sharp, wry, and widely read, she is skeptical of the sentimental way people treat sick children and keeps most of the world at a careful distance. She is devoted to a single novel about a girl with cancer and is haunted by the way it ends. Aware that her illness makes her, in her own view, a kind of hazard to those who love her, she is reluctant to form close attachments, until she is pushed by her parents to attend a cancer support group.
characters.name: Hazel Grace Lancaster

characters.description: A charming, confident seventeen-year-old whom Hazel meets at the support group. A former basketball player, he lost part of one leg to osteosarcoma and now walks on a prosthetic, and he is in remission when they meet. Witty, grandly romantic, and fond of metaphor and big gestures, he is preoccupied with the fear of being forgotten and with living a life that leaves a mark. He is quickly captivated by Hazel and shares her love of books, drawing her out of her isolation with humor and relentless warmth.
characters.name: Augustus Waters

characters.description: Augustus's best friend, a teenager with an eye cancer that has already cost him one eye and threatens the other. Facing surgery that will leave him completely blind, he is also anxious about his relationship with his girlfriend. Frank and often funny even in distress, he becomes a friend to Hazel as well, and his struggles with loss and heartbreak run alongside the central story.
characters.name: Isaac

characters.description: Hazel's devoted mother, who has organized her whole life around caring for her sick daughter. Constantly attentive and relentlessly positive, she worries over Hazel's isolation and pushes her toward the support group and toward living more fully. Beneath her cheerful, hovering presence lies a deep and constant fear for her child.
characters.name: Hazel's mother

characters.description: Hazel's loving father, a gentle, emotional man who is quick to tears and openly tender with his daughter. He supports Hazel and his wife through the strain of her illness and shares the family's mix of hope and dread.
characters.name: Hazel's father

characters.description: The reclusive American author of the novel Hazel treasures, a book about a girl with cancer that stops mid-sentence and leaves the fate of its characters unresolved. Living abroad in seclusion, he is a mystery to Hazel, who longs to know what happens after the story breaks off. Contacted through his assistant, he proves difficult and evasive, and Hazel and Augustus become determined to get answers from him in person.
characters.name: Peter Van Houten

characters.description: Peter Van Houten's assistant, a kind and conscientious woman who has arranged correspondence on his behalf. Warm and genuinely helpful, she is dismayed by her employer's behavior when Hazel and Augustus finally meet him, and she steps in to make amends and to show the young couple genuine hospitality.
characters.name: Lidewij Vliegenthart

characters.description: The earnest leader of the cancer support group Hazel attends, himself a cancer survivor who lost part of his body to the disease. He runs the meetings in a church basement with well-meaning enthusiasm, repeatedly telling his own story of survival and inviting the young members to share their fears.
characters.name: Patrick

characters.description: Isaac's girlfriend, whose relationship with him is strained as his blindness approaches. Her choices become a source of pain for Isaac and prompt one of Augustus and Hazel's shared misadventures on his behalf.
characters.name: Monica

recaps.ending: Augustus dies of his recurred cancer after a swift, harrowing decline, weeks after a mock funeral he arranged so he could hear Hazel and Isaac deliver his eulogies while he was still alive. At his real funeral, the reclusive author Peter Van Houten unexpectedly appears; afterward he tells Hazel that his own young daughter died of leukemia, which is why he wrote his novel about a dying girl and why he became the wreck she met in Amsterdam. Hazel, still angry at him, sends him away. Isaac then tells her that Augustus had been writing something in his final days. With the help of the author's assistant, Lidewij, Hazel learns that Augustus had mailed pages to Van Houten, asking the writer to shape them into a eulogy for her. Van Houten had the pages all along. When Hazel finally reads them, she finds Augustus's reflections on how people leave their marks on one another and his declaration that he was happy to love her and would choose her again despite the pain. His closing words, affirming his consent to the hurt that loving her cost him, echo her own feelings, and the novel ends with Hazel's answer that she agrees.
recaps.in_short: Hazel, a sixteen-year-old living with terminal lung cancer, meets Augustus Waters, a charming boy in remission from bone cancer, at a support group, and the two fall in love while bonding over Hazel's favorite novel, which ends abruptly and unresolved. Augustus uses his one wish to take Hazel to Amsterdam to meet the book's reclusive author, but the man turns out to be a bitter, cruel drunk who gives them no answers. The trip is redeemed by their love, and there Augustus reveals that his cancer has returned and spread; he is now dying. Back home he declines swiftly and painfully, and after a heartbreaking few weeks, including a pre-funeral he stages so he can hear his friends' eulogies, he dies. At his funeral the author appears and eventually reveals that his own daughter died of cancer, explaining his book and his bitterness. Grieving, Hazel discovers that Augustus had secretly written pages about her, intended as a eulogy, and reading his final words about their love gives her a measure of peace.

recaps.text: Hazel Grace Lancaster is a sixteen-year-old whose thyroid cancer has spread to her lungs, leaving her dependent on an oxygen tank and largely withdrawn from ordinary teenage life. Pressed by her mother to attend a cancer support group in a church basement, she meets Augustus Waters, a confident, funny seventeen-year-old in remission who lost part of a leg to bone cancer and now wears a prosthetic. He is instantly taken with her, and the two connect over their shared, ironic view of illness and, above all, over books. Hazel gives Augustus her most cherished novel, a story about a girl with cancer that ends mid-sentence and leaves its characters' fates unknown, a maddening ending she has never gotten over. Augustus reads it, is captivated, and shares her hunger to learn what happens next. Their friendship deepens quickly into something more, and Hazel, wary of hurting anyone she gets close to, finds herself drawn to him despite her caution.

Determined to learn how their beloved novel was meant to end, Hazel and Augustus track down the reclusive author's assistant and begin corresponding, eventually receiving replies that hint the writer might answer their questions in person. Meanwhile Augustus's best friend, Isaac, faces surgery that will leave him totally blind, and his girlfriend breaks up with him rather than stay through it; a distraught Isaac, with Hazel and Augustus, works out his grief and rage. Hazel and Augustus grow steadily closer even as Hazel keeps trying to guard him from the pain of loving someone as sick as she is. Then Augustus reveals a grand gift: he will spend his single wish, granted to seriously ill children, on a trip for the two of them to Amsterdam to meet the author face to face and finally get their answers.

Before the trip can happen, Hazel suffers a frightening medical crisis when fluid fills her lungs, landing her in intensive care and casting doubt on whether her doctors will clear her to travel at all. She recovers, and her team reluctantly allows the journey to go ahead, with her mother accompanying them. Hazel and Augustus fly to Amsterdam, sharing an intimate conversation on the plane about their fears and their feelings. In the city, the author's assistant has arranged a lavish, romantic dinner for the two of them at a canal-side restaurant, where they drink champagne and speak openly of their love. The evening is one of pure happiness, a brief escape from illness, as they prepare to finally meet the writer whose unfinished book brought them together.

The meeting with the author is a bitter disappointment: he turns out to be a cruel, drunken recluse who mocks them, refuses to answer any of their questions about his novel, and reduces Hazel to tears. His horrified assistant, Lidewij, quits on the spot and instead takes the couple to the Anne Frank House, where, moved and exhausted, Hazel and Augustus share their first real kiss. That night they sleep together for the first time. Soon after, Augustus confesses the reason he has seemed off: his cancer has returned and spread through his body, and this time it is terminal. He had known for some time and kept it hidden so as not to spoil their trip. The couple returns home from Amsterdam with the joy of the journey now shadowed by the certainty that Augustus is dying.

Back home, Augustus deteriorates rapidly, the confident boy Hazel fell for reduced by pain, medication, and dependence on others. In one low moment he drives out alone at night and, humiliated by a failing medical device, has to call Hazel for help. Wanting to hear how he will be remembered while he still can, Augustus stages a pre-funeral in a church, where Isaac and Hazel deliver eulogies to him directly; Hazel speaks of loving him and of the meaning found in even a short, limited life together. Not long after, Augustus dies. Hazel receives the news in the middle of the night, losing the boy who pulled her out of her isolation and taught her that a brief life could still be a full one.

At Augustus's funeral, the reclusive author unexpectedly appears, and afterward he tells Hazel that his own daughter died of cancer as a child, which is why he wrote his novel and why grief turned him into the wreck she met. Still hurt by him, Hazel refuses his overtures. Isaac then reveals that Augustus had been writing something during his final days. Following the trail through the author's assistant, Lidewij, Hazel learns that Augustus had mailed pages to the writer, asking him to turn them into a eulogy for her, and that the author had them the whole time. When Hazel finally reads Augustus's words, she finds his reflections on how people mark one another's lives and his declaration that, given the choice, he would love her all over again despite the pain it cost him. His closing affirmation of consent to that hurt mirrors her own heart, and the novel ends with her quiet agreement, a note of peace amid her grief.
